subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes, target $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + benchmark call - token volumes & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get a committed pricing proposal over to you: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Typical usage: consumer-facing chat + summarization. Rough session length ~300-600 tokens.
- Current estimated monthly tokens: 10M-30M (expected steady state). Peak/day bursts up to ~60M on major drops.
- Quality bar: preference for a high-quality open-model variant (4k context) with fallback to smaller quantized models for cost-sensitive routes.

Pricing / unit-econ items we discussed (please confirm):
1) Target unit price you'd like Redwood to hit (we asked for $/1M tokens): you mentioned aiming for a competitive number - can you confirm a range?
2) Budget range: rough monthly budget cap for inference that we should optimize for (so we can recommend batching/quant profiles).
3) Commitment term: monthly vs 12/24 month committed spend (commits materially change our price).

Benchmark context (ballpark numbers for comparison purposes only):
- OpenAI hosted (public API, hosted models): ~ $65-75 per 1M tokens for high-quality LLMs (varies by model).
- Anthropic hosted: ~ $60-70 per 1M tokens (hosted, similar tier).
- Hosted open-model providers (managed hosts of open models): ~ $35-55 per 1M tokens depending on model & optimizations.
- Self-hosted infra (raw infra + ops): often shows up as $10-30 per 1M in marginal compute for well-optimized workloads but adds ops/engineering run rate + variability.

Our initial commercial signal: for 10M-30M committed tokens we can propose a blended $/1M range of roughly $20-35 depending on the model family, committed term, and caching/batching levels. With a 12-24 month commitment we can push to the lower end.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm target $/1M range and budget cap (one-line answer).
- We share a committed-tier pricing sheet + a short example of projected monthly spend at three volume points (10M / 25M / 60M).
- If that looks aligned, we'll circulate a short commercial term sheet for legal review.

Attaching a draft commitment template and our short benchmarking slide (see attached).

Thanks -
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-commitment-draft.pdf (summary tiers), redwood-benchmarking-onepager.pdf (model cost comparison)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Intro + benchmark call - token volumes & next steps

Thanks Vanessa - good summary. A few answers/clarifications from our side: 

- Target $/1M tokens: given our budget constraints and product price sensitivity, we're targeting around $30/1M tokens as a top-line number (committed). If you can get to <$30 with a 12-month commit we'll take it seriously.
- Estimated steady usage: ~25M tokens / month. Peak can spike to ~60M/day during big feature launches (we have seasonal spikes).
- Budget range: initial procurement is budgeting $3k-$10k/mo for inference depending on drop timelines - this is flexible if the unit price comes down materially with commit terms.

We're also sensitive to latency SLAs on chat routes and need to understand fallback behavior when capacity is constrained.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up to review a committed-tier sheet.

- Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Product (AI)
ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + benchmark call - token volumes & next steps

Thanks Alex - that's really helpful. Quick notes: 

1) $30/1M target - we can definitely work toward that with a 12-month commitment at the 25M/month band; I'll ask Commercial to draft two commitment options (12-month and 24-month) and show the blended $/1M at each volume point (10M / 25M / 60M).
2) Budget: your $3k-$10k/mo band maps to the unit price target; we'll show examples that hit the $30/1M figure at the 25M committed level and show the walk-up pricing for burst usage.
3) SLA/latency: we'll include an operational note - Dedicated pools and model pinning gets you tighter latency SLOs; we'll show tradeoffs in the one-pager.

Looping in Marissa (commercial) and Aditya (solutions/benchmarking) to draft the committed-tier sheet. Can you confirm whether procurement wants an initial PO or a full SOW + PO? That will help our legal and rev ops.

Next call: are you available Fri 27 Mar 10:00am PT for a 30-minute pricing review?

Thanks -
Vanessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Committed-tier proposal (draft) - RFWD-2026-ACME-001

Hi Alex -

Attached is a draft committed-tier pricing file (redwood-pricing-commitment-draft.pdf) and a short projected monthly spend table for the volumes we discussed. Highlights (draft):

- 12-month commit (25M tokens/month avg): $30 per 1M tokens (blended) - estimated monthly spend $750. Note: blended means higher-cost model routes weighted by usage mix; we can refine once we have a per-route breakdown.
- 24-month commit: $24 per 1M tokens (blended) - estimated monthly spend $600 at 25M/month.
- Pay-as-you-go / no commit: standard hosted rates (no commit) ~ $65 per 1M tokens for the high-quality hosted model tier; we recommend a mixed strategy (pin critical routes to Dedicated, keep exploratory routes on hosted).

Security/compliance: we also included the requested security questionnaire in the drive link and attached the ACME security questionnaire you sent back filled for our info (acme-security-questionnaire.xlsx).

If the numbers above look directionally correct, we can:
- Circulate a short-term commercial term sheet for legal review (can be PO or SOW).
- Provide a short traffic-profile estimate showing how much of your traffic we'd recommend pinning to Dedicated vs hosted to hit the blended numbers.

Vanessa - I'll be ready to review on Fri 27 Mar at 10:00am PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Commercial Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-pricing-commitment-draft.pdf, acme-security-questionnaire.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Committed-tier proposal (draft) - RFWD-2026-ACME-001

Thanks Marissa - the 12-month at $30/1M and the 24-month at $24/1M look sensible as a starting point. Procurement prefers a PO + short SOW to start; we'll route the PO if legal is comfortable with the commercial term sheet.

We'll review the attachments and bring procurement into the Fri 10:00 PT call. Looking forward to the traffic-profile example.

- Alex
